text:
Alejandra: quick heads-up — noticed onboarding sample apps use three different env var names for the API key (REDWOOD_API_KEY, RW_API_TOKEN, RW_KEY). Partner got really confused during the hackweek setup.
Samir: ouch. which repos did you see that in?
Alejandra: samples/hello-embed (node) uses REDWOOD_API_KEY, docs/quickstart uses RW_API_TOKEN, and the python example in examples/semantic-search uses RW_KEY.
Samir: can you paste the snippets?
Alejandra: sure:
```bash
# node sample
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk_live_..."
# docs quickstart
export RW_API_TOKEN="sk_live_..."
# python example
os.environ['RW_KEY'] = 'sk_live_...'
```
Emily: yeah that's rough. We should standardize on REDWOOD_API_KEY (explicit) and then have separate vars for org/project: REDWOOD_ORG_ID and REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID. That keeps things clear for env-scoped CI.
Ryan: agree on names. Also: SDKs need to behave consistently when token is rotated. Right now node SDK errors with a generic 401 and python throws a different exception class. Breaks retry/backoff logic.
Samir: do we currently expose a refresh hook or a way to inject credential provider?
Emily: node+python support passing an async tokenProvider(fn) in latest alphas, but Go doesn't. Issue filed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/412 (we should add link in docs).
Alejandra: another UX problem — our CLI prints a one-off export line on `rw auth login`, but it doesn't explain expiry or rotation. People copy/paste into CI which is bad.
Ryan: we should promote ephemeral tokens + a short-lived default (1h) and a refresh flow for long-running CI via service principals. Proposal:
- env var names: REDWOOD_API_KEY (or REDWOOD_API_KEY_FILE), REDWOOD_ORG_ID, REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID
- CLI: `rw auth login --ephemeral` returns JSON with token, expiry, and snippet `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...`
- SDKs: allow tokenProvider and normalize 401 -> AuthError with `.retryable = false` so upstream can decide fallback.
Samir: +1. Also add an opt-in env var validation at SDK init that logs a warning when multiple variants are found in env (eg both RW_KEY and REDWOOD_API_KEY). That would catch a lot.
Emily: we can implement a small shared lib (go/python/node) that normalizes env reads: it checks canonical names, legacy aliases, prints guidance. Add link to migration guide.
Alejandra: any objections to making REDWOOD_API_KEY the canonical required name in docs and samples?
Ryan: none. We should also add `REDWOOD_API_KEY_ROTATE_URL` or `RW_CREDENTIALS_ENDPOINT` for org-managed rotation systems.
dev-tooling-bot: reminder: scheduled key rotation for org "redwood-test" on 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z. Reach out to security if you need exemptions.
Samir: thanks — action items I can take: create the env var normalizer lib (node + python first), add the warning hook, and open a PR to replace legacy vars in sample apps.
Emily: I'll update quickstart and the CLI `rw auth` docs to show ephemeral vs service principal flows and include sample CI snippets for token refresh.
Alejandra: I'll go through partner-facing sample repos and run a grep to list mismatches, then link PRs here.
Ryan: I'll file the SDK parity issue for Go (tokenProvider + normalized AuthError) and wire it into the release checklist.
Samir: putting a short checklist here for the docs/eng-owners: 
- standardize canonical env vars in docs/samples (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ORG_ID, REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID)
- add env-normalizer lib and warning in SDKs
- make CLI print expiry + rotate instructions and JSON output for automation
- define AuthError shape across SDKs and ensure 401 semantics are consistent
- add migration note for existing users (map legacy var names -> canonical)
Alejandra: sweet. adding `@devex` to follow. :thumbsup:
Emily: thanks y'all — will sync in docs PRs.
Ryan: if anyone wants to pair on the Go SDK change ping me.
Alejandra: closing loop — will post status updates in this thread as PRs land.
